comment: Single source of truth for the ADMIN analyst tools (RFC 0018). Mirrors shared/tool-contract.json's role for the customer surface. These tools are served by a SEPARATE process (merlins_collection.mcp_admin) and are never advertised to the customer chat — a tool the model was never told about cannot be called, and behind that the customer executor is wired to a server that does not implement them. Every tool here is read-only; nothing in this contract writes. Tools are added here as they are built, so this file and the server are always exactly equal (see backend/tests/test_admin_tool_contract.py) rather than this listing a roadmap of things that do not work yet. Every property carries a real `description` — `services/bedrock._admin_tool_schemas()` passes it straight through to the model, so a bare `{}` here is a bare `{}` in Bedrock's toolSpec too (owner report 2026-08-28: an undescribed `start`/`end` is why the analyst chat could not resolve "all time" on its own).

tools.name: get_profit_summary
tools.description: Gross sales, purchases, net and margin for a date range, optionally scoped to one show. start and end are both OPTIONAL: omit both for a wide default window covering several recent years through today (NOT guaranteed to be literally every transaction ever recorded — the response's period.start/period.end report the exact dates actually used, so read those back rather than assuming); omit just one to leave that side unbounded. Never ask the operator for exact dates when they say "all time", "everything" or "since the beginning" — just omit start and end. Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and both bounds are inclusive.

start.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive lower bound. OMIT for "all time" — never invent or ask for an exact date to mean "the beginning".

end.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive upper bound. Defaults to today when omitted.

show_id.description: Optional. Restrict the summary to one show's transactions only.

tools.name: find_aging_stock
tools.description: Held inventory that has been sitting unsold the longest, oldest first. Sold, lost and returned-to-consignor items are excluded — they are not sitting on a shelf. Optionally filter by location or by minimum value.

min_days.description: Minimum number of days an item must have been held to qualify. Defaults to 90.

location.description: Optional. Restrict to items stored at one location.

min_value.description: Optional. Only include items worth at least this much.

tools.name: get_consignor_position
tools.description: Value of stock held on each consignor's behalf, with our cut and their projected share. Archived consignors are included — archiving is not settlement. Omit consignor_id for all of them.

consignor_id.description: Optional. Restrict to one consignor's position. Omit to see every consignor.

tools.name: find_pricing_outliers
tools.description: Held stock whose asking price disagrees with the market figure. direction is 'over' (asking above market), 'under' (below), or 'unpriced' (no asking price). threshold_pct is a magnitude — direction alone decides the sign.

direction.description: 'over' = priced above market, 'under' = priced below market, 'unpriced' = no asking price at all (ignores threshold_pct).

threshold_pct.description: Magnitude of the deviation threshold, as a percent (e.g. 20 means 20%). Defaults to 20. Ignored when direction is 'unpriced'.

tools.name: list_shows
tools.description: Every show with its date/venue and, when available, its analytics snapshot (gross sales, purchases, net, item counts), newest first. A show that has never been archived or manually analyzed has has_analytics=false and null money fields — that is not the same as a show with zero sales; say so rather than treating it as unprofitable. If limit truncates the result, you are seeing the most RECENT shows, not a representative sample of all of them.

start.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Omit for all shows regardless of date.

end.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Omit for all shows regardless of date.

include_archived.description: Defaults to true — most real shows are archived, and archiving is not settlement (CLAUDE.md). Set false to see only currently-active shows.

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.description: Raw ledger rows in a date range. NEVER sum `amount` across these rows to state a profit/revenue/gross figure — call get_profit_summary instead (trade cash legs double-count and voided rows must be excluded; both are flagged per-row here so you can filter, but the aggregate tools already do it correctly). Use this to browse, filter, or answer questions the aggregate tools do not cover.

start.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Omit for the wide default window (see get_profit_summary's start for the same behavior).

end.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Defaults to today.

show_id.description: Optional. Restrict to one show's transactions.

type.description: Optional. Restrict to one transaction type.

include_voided.description: Defaults to false. When true, voided rows are included, each still carrying voided_at and is_countable=false — never treat one as a real transaction.

sort.description: Optional, e.g. 'amount_desc'. Same fields as GET /admin/transactions's sort.

limit.description: Maximum rows returned, capped at 100. total_matched/truncated in the response tell you if you need to narrow the range instead of raising this.

tools.name: list_inventory
tools.description: Raw inventory rows with admin-only fields (cost basis, consignment terms, review flags) the customer-facing inventory tools never expose. Prices here are RAW figures, not customer-facing condition-adjusted prices. A row's consignment field is non-null when the item is held for someone else — exclude those rows before summing cost_basis as the business's own capital, the same way get_consignor_position already does for consignment value. Narrow with filters — the table is the largest in the system and results are capped.

filters.description: Each string is 'field:op:value', identical to the admin inventory page's ?filter= parameter (e.g. 'status:eq:available', 'cost_basis:gte:100'). See FILTERABLE_FIELDS for the full field list; op is one of contains/eq/gte/lte/isnull/notnull.

sort.description: Optional, e.g. 'cost_basis_desc'. Same fields as the admin inventory page's sort.

tools.name: list_consignors
tools.description: Every consignor's identity and default payout_percent (THEIR share as a percent, e.g. 50 = 50% — the OPPOSITE convention from an item's ConsignmentTerms.split_percent, which is OUR cut as a 0-1 fraction). Do not use this to compute anyone's payout — call get_consignor_position for a correct, item-level projected split. Use this for identity/contact/archived-status questions.

include_archived.description: Defaults to true — archiving is not settlement (CLAUDE.md), so an archived consignor may still be owed money.
